title: Your Wallet: Keys and Addresses
objectives: Understand the difference between public keys and private keys
Learn why a seed phrase can recreate your entire wallet
Discover how digital signatures prove ownership without revealing secrets

steps.title: Public vs Private: The Postbox Analogy
steps.body:
Think of a crypto <Term id="wallet">wallet</Term> like a high-security postbox with two completely different sides.

**The front slot: your public identity.** Your <Term id="public_key">public key</Term> (usually shortened into an <Term id="address">address</Term> like `7xKX...9dQ`) is the slot on the front of the box. Anyone in the world can drop letters or tokens through it. It is completely safe to share with friends, exchanges, or websites - publishing it invites payments, it never risks them.

**The back door: your private key.** Your <Term id="private_key">private key</Term> is the only key that unlocks the back of the box to take things out. Whoever holds it *is* you as far as the blockchain is concerned. If someone copies your private key, they can empty your box in seconds, with no refund and no reversal.

**The mental model that prevents 90% of hacks:** an address is a *destination*, a private key is *ownership*. You hand out destinations all day. You never, ever hand out ownership.

steps.title: The Master Key: Your Seed Phrase
steps.body:
When you install Phantom or Solflare, you are given a 12 or 24-word <Term id="seed_phrase">seed phrase</Term> like *'ripple canyon velvet ...'*.

**Why 12 words hold an entire wallet.** That sequence is not a random password stored on a server. It is a mathematical seed. From those words, your wallet deterministically derives every private key and every address you will ever use. Anyone who has the seed phrase can regenerate your whole wallet on any device, anywhere.

**Three rules that will keep you safe:**
- Write it on paper or stamp it into metal. Never screenshot it, never store it in Notes, Photos, or cloud drives.
- **Never type your seed phrase into any website, Discord form, or Google Doc.**
- Real wallet popups will **NEVER** ask you to re-enter your seed phrase to approve a transaction. If a page asks, it is a drainer - close it instantly.

Remember: losing your seed phrase loses the wallet. Leaking it gives the wallet away. There is no 'forgot password' link in self-custody.

steps.title: Under the Hood: How Signing Works
steps.body: When you approve an action, your wallet uses the Ed25519 elliptic-curve algorithm to combine your private key with the transaction message. This produces a unique 64-byte cryptographic <Term id="signature">signature</Term>. Anyone on the network can mathematically verify using your public key that the signature was created by your private key, without ever seeing or deducing the private key itself.

questions.prompt: Which of these is safe to share publicly with someone sending you tokens?
questions.explainRight: Correct! Your public key / address is meant to be shared so people can send you tokens.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. Only your public key (address) can be shared. Private keys and seed phrases must stay 100% secret.

questions.prompt: If a website asks you to enter your seed phrase to 'verify your wallet' or 'claim an airdrop', what should you do?
options: Enter it quickly before the airdrop expires
Close the tab immediately. It is a scam drainer trying to steal your funds
Send it to a support agent on Telegram
questions.explainRight: 100% right! Legitimate Web3 dapps never ask for your seed phrase. That is always a phishing drainer.
questions.explainWrong: Never enter your seed phrase! Any site asking for your seed words is trying to steal your wallet.
